chapters.title: How to use the visual labs

text: See it. Trace it. Predict it.

A diagram becomes useful when you can explain what changes inside it. Each chapter now has two complete visual labs. The A lab connects the chapter analogy to a concrete mechanism. The B lab applies it to a case you can inspect.
See: Name the records, actors, permissions or quantities in the picture. Read the starting conditions before following a line.
Trace: Follow the three numbered reading cues. Identify what changed and what stayed true. A green cell marks a changed field; a PASS or ALLOW label states a decision.
Predict: Answer the question in the dark strip. Say which visible fact supports your answer. Then use the answer link to check your reasoning.

Numbered routes are matched to their route log. A denied route ends at a stop mark. Lines in a time lane show event order, not elapsed duration. Numeric bars and capacity trays use proportional lengths. An interval shows uncertainty around a measured proportion in a constructed sample.

Every lab states its assumptions. A real system needs the contracts and checks discussed in the chapter; a drawn boundary cannot enforce them. Status words and symbols accompany colour, so the important decisions remain visible in monochrome.

Use the separate visual atlas for a diagram-first review. Return to the full chapter for the detailed reasoning, code and exercises. Prediction answers appear in Appendix H of the full book and at the end of the atlas.

32A. If the child subgraph returns its received E-17 plus E-17 again, how many entries should remain?

No. A valid citation can still be insufficient for its claim. The receipt supports that rollback applied, not that service recovery criteria passed. Obtain the complete authorized post-action observation window and required dependency checks, or report the narrower applied-but-unverified status.

35A. If investigation uses an agent, may it choose to skip the mandatory refund approval?

No. The adaptive investigator returns evidence and a proposal to the fixed procedure. Eligibility, required authority and effect recovery remain deterministic boundaries. Adding an agent inside one part of the workflow does not transfer control of its mandatory gates to the model.

No. That would remove capacity for a required completion check. Omit the optional critic or use a separately qualified option that fits. If verification cannot be funded, report a bounded incomplete outcome. Simplification should cut machinery without removing the evidence contract that makes the result trustworthy.
36A. At 10:10, may the commander announce verified recovery because RB-82 applied at 10:09?

No. Only one post-action minute has elapsed. The required ten-minute covered window and the alert, dependency and new-failure checks must pass. Report rollback applied and verification pending. An applied receipt proves the command outcome under its contract, not the incident outcome.

No. That changes the proposal's bound assumptions and canonical arguments. Reinvestigate current state and create a new proposal with its required approval. Preserve P-9 and its conflict outcome for audit. A hash match or valid approver cannot authorize an edited action.

No. A read can expose another service or tenant, and outbound queries can disclose private context. No. Another deployment can occur after the last read. Pass the expected revision to a service that checks it atomically with mutation, or use an equivalent supported conditional-write contract. On conflict, refresh evidence and obtain authority for any changed proposal.

No. The two-sided 95% Wilson upper bound is about 8.76% under the stated sampling model. Deliberately curated attacks may not satisfy that model at all. Preserve zero observed forbidden effects as a hard test gate, add threat coverage and rehearsal, and do not interpret uncertainty as permission to tolerate violations.

No. It demonstrates the injected case under that fake provider's specified deduplication behavior.
